title: Lagaria Unveils Platea: A 90-Metre Concept Redefining Outdoor Living
description: Lagaria reveals Platea, a 90-metre motor yacht concept designed around outdoor living and social spaces.
html:
Monaco Design Studio Presents Bold New Motor Yacht Concept Centered On Expansive Deck Spaces

Monaco-based design studio Lagaria has unveiled Platea, a striking 90-metre motor yacht concept that places outdoor living at the heart of its design philosophy. The vessel represents a thoughtful departure from conventional superyacht layouts, prioritizing expansive deck areas and seamless transitions between interior and exterior spaces that encourage guests to spend time in the Mediterranean sun.

The concept emerged from Lagaria’s conviction that modern yacht owners increasingly value the ability to entertain and relax in open-air environments. Rather than maximizing interior volume, Platea allocates substantial deck real estate to lounging areas, dining spaces, and social zones that take full advantage of the vessel’s proportions. This philosophy extends across multiple deck levels, creating a hierarchy of outdoor experiences from intimate forward spaces to expansive aft entertaining areas. At 90 metres in length, Platea offers a compelling platform for owners seeking a balance between intimate cruising and the capacity to host larger gatherings. The design emphasizes flow and connectivity, with carefully considered sightlines that allow guests to move naturally between different outdoor zones while maintaining visual connection to the sea. Large sliding glass panels and retractable awnings provide flexibility, allowing owners to adapt spaces to changing weather and personal preferences throughout the day.

The exterior profile reflects contemporary aesthetics while maintaining the classic proportions that define successful superyachts. Clean lines and minimal ornamentation create a refined silhouette, with the superstructure positioned to maximize unobstructed views from key entertaining areas. The hull design incorporates modern hydrodynamic principles, ensuring efficient cruising performance while maintaining the stability required for comfortable extended voyages. Interior spaces, though secondary to the outdoor focus, have been thoughtfully conceived to serve as comfortable retreats during inclement weather or evening hours. The main saloon features generous glazing that frames views of the surrounding seascape, while the owner’s suite and guest accommodations are positioned to capture natural light and maintain visual connection to the water. Lagaria’s interior approach emphasizes materiality and craftsmanship, with natural finishes and refined detailing creating warm, residential atmospheres.

From a technical perspective, Platea is conceived as a fully capable cruising vessel. The concept incorporates modern propulsion systems designed for efficiency and reduced environmental impact, with integrated energy management systems that support extended range and autonomous operation. Lagaria has specified redundancy in critical systems, ensuring reliability for owners planning extended voyages to remote destinations. The 90-metre size positions Platea within a segment increasingly favored by discerning owners who value maneuverability and operational flexibility alongside the space and amenities expected of larger vessels. This scale allows for efficient crew management while providing sufficient volume for comprehensive guest accommodations, crew quarters, and technical systems.

Lagaria’s design team has incorporated flexibility into the concept, recognizing that individual owners will have distinct preferences regarding accommodation layouts, technical specifications, and interior finishes. The modular approach to interior planning allows for customization without compromising the core design philosophy centered on outdoor living and seamless indoor-outdoor transitions. The unveiling of Platea reflects broader trends within the superyacht industry toward designs that prioritize lifestyle and experience over pure interior volume. As owners increasingly seek vessels suited to extended cruising and entertaining in diverse environments, concepts like Platea demonstrate how thoughtful design can enhance the fundamental appeal of yacht ownership. For prospective owners interested in exploring how this concept might be adapted to their specific requirements, Lagaria remains available to discuss custom variations and build partnerships with shipyards capable of realizing the design at full scale.
